# CommonMark 0.31.2 conformance suite

`spec.json` is the official machine-readable test suite for CommonMark 0.31.2,
extracted from the specification text. 652 cases across 26 sections.

- **Source:** <https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/spec.json>
- **SHA-256:** `d431b29d97b6f73e69d547109cf5081578fac931e72afe95639ebe766c1b2a20`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/commonmark/commonmark-spec>
- **Copyright:** © 2014–2016 John MacFarlane
- **License:** **CC-BY-SA 4.0** — <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/>

## Why this file is committed rather than fetched

Sherd's tests must run with the network interface down. That is not a
convenience preference — it is the same property design principle 4
("offline-complete") demands of the application, and it should hold for the
project's own build. Fetching the suite at test time would make CI, and every
contributor's first `make check`, depend on `spec.commonmark.org` being
reachable.

## Licensing

CC-BY-SA 4.0 is **one-way compatible with GPL-3.0**: Creative Commons
explicitly permits CC BY-SA 4.0 material to be incorporated into a GPLv3 work.
Sherd is GPL-3.0-or-later, so including this file is permitted, and `LEG-002`
is satisfied — this is a third-party asset under a compatible license, with
attribution.

Obligations that come with it, and how they are met:

| Obligation | How |
|---|---|
| Attribution | This file, plus an entry in the repository `NOTICE` |
| Indicate changes | The file is committed **unmodified**; the harness reads it as-is |
| ShareAlike | Sherd is GPL-3.0-or-later, which CC accepts as a compatible adaptation licence |

**Do not edit this file.** Sherd-specific cases go in
`testdata/conformance/sherd/`. Editing the vendored suite would both break the
"unmodified" basis above and silently weaken `FR-MD-001`, which requires the
CommonMark suite passing at 100%.
